contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #282: From scale symmetry to local conformal symmetry in four-dimensional QFT.
Settle the separated subtraction implication D:subtractions and D:two-horizon on compact positive output-mass tests, without promoting its unreviewed QFT premises to proved results.

definitions.separated: P_q(q,r)+P_r(q,r), polynomial in q or in r respectively, with one finite degree bound and arbitrary coefficients in the other variable
definitions.H: the internal Hilbert space L^2(R_+,M dM) with finitely many polarization labels
definitions.premise_faithful: an obstruction must satisfy every premise of the particular implication it refutes

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 282 (From scale symmetry to local conformal symmetry in four-dimensional QFT.; papers: Scale and conformal symmetry in four-dimensional operational quantum field theory; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Manuscript ass:framework supplies a vacuum-generated operational Wightman QFT, locality, positive spectrum, Poincare and dilation covariance, finite-multiplicity discrete homogeneous field decompositions and the fixed affiliated local net. This is an assumption, not a verified theorem.

Manuscript thm:main claims that ass:framework yields a physical dimension-two improvement scalar in the original local theory, a symmetric conserved traceless improved stress tensor preserving affine charges, and local conformal symmetry. Unreviewed manuscript conclusion.

Manuscript F:old-domain and F:strip-comparison lead to F:spectral-comparison, the spectral-subspace comparison between the parabolic operator and the regular Hankel realizations in each polarization. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript N:Ward-proposition, N:measure-proposition and N:moment-comparison yield D:measure-input: H_g=b integral g(Y+z) mu(dz), mu(1)=id, mu(z_i)=0, kappa=mu(|z|^2)<=h, with the stated commutation and covariance properties. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript D:plane-matrix identifies the spacelike-transfer full-plane stress matrix with the bounded-profile measure matrix, including the claimed fixed-normal pullback. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript D:causal-continuation asserts one covariant split commutator whose fixed-positive-virtuality upper/lower half-plane values have uniform finite polynomial growth, whose jumps have the specified Wightman spectral support and relative sign, and whose two spacelike gap values agree. Unreviewed manuscript dependency, stronger than local extension alone.

Manuscript D:jump identifies both jumps, with the same nonzero normalization, with [mu_n(q)(M^2+|r|^2)^2 c_T^(bar n)(M,r) phi(-M^2)] in the adapted spin-one output frame. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

D:subtractions: There are continuous L^2(M dM)-valued regularizations chi_reg^n(r,M) of chi^n(r,M)=(M^2+|r|^2)c_T^(bar n)(M,r) such that, with A_A=[mu_n(q)chi_reg^n(r)]_{j_A^(n)} and B_A=[mu_bar_n(r)chi_reg^bar_n(q)]_{j_A^(bar_n)}, (M_o^2+|q+r|^2)A_z-(|q+r|^2-M_o^2)B_z+2M_o(q_i+r_i)B_i=P_q+P_r. The degree of each polynomial is uniformly finite. The coefficients of P_q, polynomial in q, may depend on r; those of P_r, polynomial in r, may depend on q.

For a common-order Cauchy subtraction of a finite Lorentz tensor family, covariance under the null rotations r->r+b beta preserving q,X,z,M_o,b forces every zero-jump subtraction polynomial, evaluated at z=|r|^2, to have uniformly finite polynomial degree in r. This is the delicate implication to prove or obstruct.

The explicit cutoff prescription in D:subtractions produces continuous H-valued waves; for every sufficiently large integer subtraction order d, their difference from the Cauchy-regulated wave is an H-valued polynomial in r of uniformly finite degree.

Under the exact common-gap and common-jump premises, the null-rotation polynomial remainder and H-valued regularization imply D:two-horizon with a uniform separated polynomial remainder, including at the transverse axes by continuity.

There exists a covariant, causally split, spectrally admissible matrix satisfying the precise D:subtractions premises but violating its separated-polynomial conclusion. This is an unresolved alternative route, not a claim that a counterexample has been found.
Manuscript D:radial-identity follows by annihilating the separated ambiguities with two annular transverse tests and exchanging the two horizons. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript D:exact-tail gives a single lambda^-2 exterior tail with d_jz=-d_l and d_sz=-d_l/3, using the Hankel order-transfer identity and inherited spectral comparisons. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript D:plateau-estimates establishes uniform edge estimates, the nonzero plateau normalization c_*=24, and the weighted tail expansion needed for logarithmic pairing. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript D:critical-comparison uses D:radial-identity, positivity and logarithmic pairing to force d_l=0 and the order-zero scalar spectral comparison D:order-zero. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.
Manuscript C:single-insertion, C:canonical-Pi and C:Q-zero supply local charge forms and eliminate the residual dilation charge. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.
Manuscript C:cone-modularity and C:time-mobius identify actual cone modular groups and time-Mobius action from the charge forms and half-sided modular input. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript E:accessible-scalar, E:bounded-approximation and E:accessible-products construct the dimension-two scalar wave S and localized bounded approximants and products. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.
Manuscript P:short-products, P:pair-representation and P:return use short-product positivity and conformal pair data to identify the formal trace wave l with S. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript R:mixed-products, R:pure-products, R:causal-solution and R:affiliation reconstruct all finite products, a common invariant domain and affiliation in the original net. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Manuscript R:improvement, R:Ward-Lie and R:compatible-families construct the physical improvement scalar, improved tensor and conformal Ward action for admitted families. Unreviewed manuscript dependency.

Finite-order causal distributions admit retarded/advanced extensions with prescribed support; finite-order splitting ambiguities are supported at the origin and hence finite delta jets. External local-extension result, not a theorem about the present fixed-output restrictions.

The classical Fourier-Laplace theorem identifies tempered distributions supported in a proper convex cone with holomorphic slowly increasing tube functions having tempered boundary values. It does not by itself establish the manuscript fixed-null-normal pullback.

Known obstruction to an on-shell shortcut: vanishing dilaton amplitudes need not remove semi-local correlator contributions, and such contributions can support the three- and four-point scale anomaly. This does not establish a nonseparated ambiguity under D:subtractions premises.

claims.natural_statement: For a finite Lorentz tensor family of total rank t, a common-order Cauchy zero-jump remainder polynomial in z of uniform degree e and equivariant under null rotations fixing n is polynomial in r after z=|r|^2, of degree at most 2t+2+2e including the adapted spin-one frame contraction. The coefficients may depend on q.

For every integer d>=2, every z0>0 and every real transverse r, the manuscript cutoff wave chi_reg and chi_C,d=chi((|r|^2-z0)/(-M^2-z0))^d are continuous L^2(M dM)-valued functions of r; chi_C,d-chi_reg is an H-valued polynomial in r of degree at most 2d+2. The exact mass tail and all-order quotient identity are given in research/two_horizon_subtractions/proof.md.

Assuming precisely D:causal-continuation and D:jump with a common nonzero normalization and the stated bounded positive-measure Fourier matrices, the cutoff prescription satisfies D:two-horizon on all real q,r. A conservative uniform total-degree bound is max(2t+2+2e,2d+2,3)+2 for raw tensor rank t, z-remainder degree e and common Cauchy order d>=2. No verification of the upstream QFT premises is asserted.

external_assumptions.statement: The classical Fourier-Laplace cone/tube equivalence for tempered distributions supplies the half-line Fourier support of polynomially bounded upper and lower half-plane boundary values. Their common zero-jump boundary therefore has Fourier support at zero.

routes.retired_because: The conditional theorem in research/two_horizon_subtractions/proof.md proves that every zero-jump remainder from the same finite covariant tensor family has a polynomial null-rotation orbit in r, and the all-order H-valued replacement preserves separation. Hence an obstruction satisfying all those precise premises cannot exist. This does not exclude failure of D:causal-continuation or D:jump upstream; independent Reviewer confirmation is pending.
Bzowski-Skenderis arXiv:1402.3208v4 Section 1 explains why vanishing on-shell dilaton amplitudes does not eliminate semi-local anomaly terms; this cannot supply the local trace identity.
